qualitative.gate_2_reason: Budget hotel accommodation is non-essential and subject to discretionary travel cycles that are easily forgone during economic downturns.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 2 (Rejected – G2 Essential Need). Whitbread operates the Premier Inn budget hotel chain; budget lodging is non-essential and subject to discretionary leisure and business travel cycles that are cut during economic recessions.
qualitative.evidence: Whitbread operates >85k rooms under Premier Inn, largely through a capital-intensive freehold/leasehold owner-operator model. Its ROCE/ROIC hovers around 8-11%, depressed by heavy real estate assets and German expansion capex. End-market lodging demand is cyclical and discretionary, failing Gate 2 essential need requirements.
